findings.fix: Recast Step 2.1 as a short decision table (flags → target → which gate question, with which answers) and keep the full prose. The process pattern then reads as checkpoints instead of dense paragraphs.

findings.evidence: The description is 1013 of 1024 characters, mostly implementation mechanics such as "asks each role's order, effort and opt-in flags, and writes the [lanes] table", and leaves almost no room for later edits
findings.fix: Use this skill to set up, refresh or check ai-kit's cross-AI lanes: which models review plans, which implement them, and each role's fallback order. Use when the user wants cross-AI review or execute lanes set up, refreshed or checked, wants a second-vendor reviewer or a fallback executor, when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers reports that no lanes exist, to find lane providers opencode no longer lists, or to migrate an old review-spec.toml, even without the word lanes. Writes the [lanes] table of ./.aikit/config.toml (or the user config.toml with --global) and asks before it replaces a roster. --check-only reports availability and writes nothing. Not for running a review or execute with configured lanes, hand-editing one lane value, or editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.
